subject: Re: Marketplace procurement questionnaire & data residency / SLA clarifications
messages:
From: Natalie Green <natalie.green@bluepeak.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@bluepeak.com
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Marketplace procurement questionnaire and onboarding checklist

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. BluePeak's procurement team asked me to send the marketplace procurement questionnaire and a short list of clarifying items we need answered before we proceed to legal/finance. Our timeline is tight — we'd like to complete the vendor technical/contracting review this week so we can include Redwood in the AWS listing project.

High-level asks:
- Confirm data residency options for customer-managed deployments (US regions) and whether private deployments can be isolated in a customer's VPC.
- Provide a draft SLA with uptime and latency SLOs, and your planned remedy/credits model (we can share thresholds).
- Tell us how metering/entitlement works on AWS Marketplace and whether Redwood supports consolidated billing vs. direct invoicing.
- SOC 2 / audit evidence (we need a redacted attestation for our compliance team).
- Any marketplace packaging constraints (AMI, SaaS subscription, or container listing) — preference is for a SaaS listing with metered usage, but we need to know options.

I've attached the questionnaire and an internal procurement checklist (attachment: BluePeak_marketplace_questionnaire_20261120.xlsx). Please reply with the requested attachments or a short call if needed.

Best,
Natalie Green
Procurement Manager | BluePeak Technologies
(attachment stub: BluePeak_marketplace_questionnaire_20261120.xlsx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Natalie Green <natalie.green@bluepeak.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-20T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace procurement questionnaire and onboarding checklist

Hi Natalie — thanks for sending this over and for the time yesterday.

Quick answers and attachments are below; Laura (Solutions Engineering) and Rachel (Commercial Operations) are looped to pick up technical and billing/marketplace details respectively.

Attachments included: Redwood_Marketplace_Security_Annex.pdf, SLA_Draft_20261120.docx, SOC2_Type2_Attestation_2025.pdf (redacted).

Short summary:
- Data residency: For Redwood Private (VPC) we support deployment into customer VPCs in all major US regions; data can be configured to remain in-region and we provide controls for KMS key ownership. For Hosted SaaS we offer region-specific tenancy in us-east-1 and us-west-2; we can sign data processing addenda for EU/US controls if required.
- Private deployment isolation: yes — Private supports full network isolation and optional customer-managed NAT/GW and routing.
- SLA & remedies: The attached draft outlines 99.95% uptime for Dedicated and a 99.9% availability target for Hosted API; latency SLOs are page 2 (p95 targets by model class). Remedies are credits proportional to downtime windows; commercial exceptions can be discussed in contract.
- Marketplace metering & billing: Redwood supports SaaS metered listings via AWS Marketplace (usage-based metering token) and also supports contracts that use consolidated invoicing or direct billing depending on buyer preference and channel. Rachel can outline flow for committed pricing vs. pay-as-you-go.
- Packaging: We can list as a SaaS subscription with metered usage (recommended). AMI or container listings are available for on-prem variants but add lead time.

If you prefer, we can jump on a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk procurement through each attachment.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
(attachment stubs: Redwood_Marketplace_Security_Annex.pdf, SLA_Draft_20261120.docx, SOC2_Type2_Attestation_2025.pdf)

Date: 2026-11-21T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace procurement questionnaire and onboarding checklist

Hi Natalie — Laura from Solutions Engineering here. A few technical clarifications to add to Karthik's note:

1) VPC/on-prem model: for Private installs we provide a drop-in control plane that runs in Redwood's management plane but all inference workloads and model artifacts can be pinned to customer-owned infrastructure. Customer KMS/HSM integration is supported for key wrapping.

2) Network egress and telemetry: we can suppress telemetry to Redwood endpoints if required for an air-gapped installation; by default we ship aggregated anonymized metrics for cost/ops visibility.

3) Operational runbook & marketplace integration: we will provide runbooks for provisioning metering keys and configuring entitlements in the AWS console. Typical lead time for a SaaS listing with metering is 2–3 weeks after legal signoff; AMI/container options typically add 4–6 weeks for packaging and security scanning.

Happy to schedule a 30-min technical onboarding with your cloud ops and security teams.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
(attachment: Redwood_Marketplace_Security_Annex.pdf)

Karthik / Laura — thanks, this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups the compliance team flagged after reviewing your SOC 2 attestation and the security annex:

- Can you confirm log retention and audit log export options for Private deployments (we need 365+ days and an S3-hosted export option)?
- For the SLA, our legal team asks whether availability credits are capped (we typically accept up to 6 months' credits for SaaS listings) — is that acceptable?
- Marketplace billing: our procurement prefers consolidated billing via AWS Marketplace for a single invoice across several vendors. If Redwood can be configured for consolidated invoicing that will simplify internal approvals.

Would you be able to provide explicit wording for the above items we can include in our procurement worksheet? If so, please send by COB Monday so we can move to legal review.

Best,
Natalie

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Natalie Green <natalie.green@bluepeak.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T10:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace procurement questionnaire and onboarding checklist

Hi Natalie — Rachel from Commercial Ops here. Thanks for the detailed questions — answers and wording you can copy into your procurement worksheet below.

1) Audit logs & retention (Private deployments):
- Retention: Redwood Private ships an audit export capability that can be configured to retain logs for 365 days by default; we support customer-owned S3 buckets for export and an automated lifecycle rule can be applied from provisioning. Wording for your worksheet: "Redwood will support audit log export to a customer-provided S3 bucket and retain exported logs for a period of at least 365 days. Access controls and encryption are managed according to customer KMS policies."

2) SLA credit cap:
- Standard: Availability credits are calculated pro-rata and are capped at 3 months' subscription charges for Hosted SaaS by default.
- Contract carveout: For enterprise deals, Redwood is willing to negotiate credit caps up to 6 months' charges subject to contract and commercial review. Wording: "Availability credits are calculated pro-rata based on service downtime and applied to future invoices. Standard credit cap is three (3) months of subscription fees; up to six (6) months may be negotiated for enterprise agreements."

3) Consolidated billing via AWS Marketplace:
- Redwood supports consolidated billing when customers purchase via AWS Marketplace — we can enable consolidation through marketplace procurement flow. Note: some multi-year committed pricing options may require a direct invoicing clause; we can accommodate both. Wording: "Redwood supports consolidated billing through AWS Marketplace for eligible purchases; customers requiring committed invoicing terms may opt for direct invoicing under a separate commercial agreement."

Next steps: If the above covers your workbook, we'll update the deal in HubSpot (link included) and Rachel will send a short checklist of required marketplace admin roles to provision metering keys. Happy to review with your legal team next week.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
